title: Myth flip — 3 a.m. wake-ups aren't 'just stress' (Reena, 44)
caption:
Myth: 3 a.m. wake-ups are “just stress.” In perimenopause sleep breaks years before hot flashes (NIA). Insomnia doubles the odds of later depression (Baglioni 2011). Ask for CBT-I first (AASM 2021).
Which myth next? 👇
www.aiforheratx.org
#perimenopause #womenshealth #insomnia #cbti #menopausesleep

scenes.text: “It's just *stress*.” Reena, 44, has been waking at 3:41 for a year and a half.
Four people told her to try chamomile. Nobody asked what her sleep was actually doing.
phrases: It's been 18 months. It hasn't passed.

scenes.text: In perimenopause, sleep usually breaks *years* before the first hot flash (NIA).
phrases: So she started reading at 4 a.m.
Hot flashes, if they come, come later.

scenes.text: Untreated insomnia roughly doubles the odds of depression later. Sleep sits upstream of mood (Baglioni, 2011).

scenes.text: Ten minutes of worry-writing at 8 p.m., out of bed. Then ask her clinician for CBT-I.
phrases: 8 p.m.: 10-minute worry list, at the kitchen table.
Ask your clinician for *CBT-I* — the 6-week sleep retraining (AASM 2021).
Aim for 150 minutes of moderate movement a week (WHO).
